faqs.question: What should ITSM software include?
faqs.answer: Requirements often include incident and service-request handling, routing, priorities, approvals, knowledge, reporting, and audit history. Change management, asset tracking, and service catalogs may also matter depending on the organization.

faqs.question: Are prices and ratings verified?
faqs.answer: No. Current prices, ratings, and plan limits have not been independently verified. Confirm the exact product edition and modules with the vendor.

faqs.question: Can project-management tools replace ITSM software?
faqs.answer: They may coordinate project work, but do not assume they provide formal incident queues, service catalogs, service targets, change approvals, or audit controls. Verify each required workflow.

faqs.question: How should I test an ITSM platform?
faqs.answer: Run a representative incident and service request through intake, routing, escalation, resolution, reporting, and audit review. Include permissions and a failed handoff.

faqs.question: What costs should I include?
faqs.answer: Include agents or user seats, modules, automation, integrations, implementation, support, and the time required to maintain workflows and knowledge.

author: Marcus Rivera
body:
IT Service Management Tools: A Practical Buyer’s Guide

IT service management (ITSM) tools help teams manage incidents, service requests, changes, assets, approvals, and internal knowledge. General project-management boards may track tasks, but they may not provide the service catalog, incident history, or governance required for IT operations.

Transparency note: Current prices, ratings, plan limits, and product claims have not been independently verified. Confirm current feature availability and pricing with vendors before choosing.

Tools to evaluate

Asana

Evaluate Asana for coordinating IT projects and follow-up work. Test task ownership, deadlines, dependencies, and reporting, while checking whether formal incident, service-request, and change-management workflows need a dedicated ITSM product.

monday.com

Evaluate monday.com for configurable request and project boards. Test forms, routing, approvals, permissions, and reporting, and confirm whether the product meets your ITSM governance and audit requirements.

Smartsheet

Evaluate Smartsheet for structured tracking and reporting of service work. Test intake, ownership, escalation, approvals, and how records are audited and reported. Confirm whether ITSM-specific workflows require other tools.

Wrike

Evaluate Wrike for coordinating complex work across teams. Test request intake, workload visibility, dependencies, and reporting. Confirm whether incident queues, service catalogs, and change approvals are supported in the way your IT team needs.

Jira

Evaluate Jira and its service-management capabilities for request queues, incident handling, workflows, permissions, and knowledge links. Confirm which product edition and modules are required for the service processes you need.

Confluence

Evaluate Confluence for internal knowledge, runbooks, and service documentation. Test search, permissions, page ownership, change history, and links to incident or service records. It is typically a knowledge component rather than a full ticketing system on its own.

ITSM evaluation checklist

  1. Define incident, service-request, change, and escalation workflows.
  2. Test intake, routing, priority, ownership, service targets, and audit history.
  3. Review role permissions, knowledge links, asset records, and reporting.
  4. Check integrations with identity, monitoring, endpoint, and communication systems.
  5. Test data export and recovery for tickets, attachments, and knowledge pages.
  6. Compare seats, modules, automation, integrations, support, and implementation.

Methodology

This is an evaluation guide, not a verified ranking. Confirm that the selected product provides the ITSM controls your organization needs; task boards and documentation tools are not automatically substitutes for service management.
